{{Infobox election | election_name = United States House of Representatives election in Delaware, At-large district, 2018 | country = Delaware | type = presidential | ongoing = no | previous_election = United States House of Representatives election in Delaware, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives election in Delaware, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | election_date = November 6, 2018 | image1 = [[File:Lisa Blunt Rochester official photo (cropped).jpg|x150px]] | candidate1 = [[Lisa Blunt Rochester]] | party1 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = [[File:3x4.svg|x150px]] | candidate2 = Scott Walker | party2 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | map_image = | map_size = | map_caption = | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Lisa Blunt Rochester]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{ElectionsDE}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives election in Delaware''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the U.S. Representative from [[Delaware's at-large congressional district]], who will represent the state of [[Delaware]] in the [[116th United States Congress]]. The election will coincide with the election of [[United States Senate election in Delaware, 2018|a U.S. Senator from Delaware]] and other federal and state offices. The seat is currently held by Democratic Congresswoman [[Lisa Blunt Rochester]]. ==Democratic primary== Lisa Blunt Rochester ran unopposed in the primary and automatically became the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic ]] nominee. ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[Lisa Blunt Rochester]], incumbent U.S. Representative{{cite web|url=https://elections.delaware.gov/reports/genl_fcddt.shtml|title=FILED CANDIDATES BY OFFICE|work=Delaware Department of Elections}} ====Withdrew==== * Rose Izzo, [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] candidate for the seat in [[United States House of Representatives election in Delaware, 2016|2016]], [[United States House of Representatives election in Delaware, 2014|2014]], and [[United States House of Representatives election in Delaware, 2012|2012]] (ran for [[Delaware House of Representatives|State House]] in district 7) ====Declined==== * [[Kerri Evelyn Harris]], [[Dover, Delaware|Dover]] activist and [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] veteran (ran for U.S. Senate) ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box |title=Lisa Blunt Rochester |list= ;Organizations {{Election box end}} ===Controversy=== Shortly afer the final results for the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] primary, controversy almost immediately emerged about Scott Walker’s victory, as Lee Murphy had been seen as many as the favorite to win. Murphy refused to concede and took to [[Facebook]] in saying, “Friends, thanks for all your support- something stinks here and I will not be conceding anytime soon. Need to investigate big time. A Dem wins a Republican primary?”{{cite web|title=Matthew Bittle on Twitter|url=https://twitter.com/matthewcbittle/status/1038068786237190145?s=21}} Murphy also called for an investigation into the results.{{cite web|title=Lee Murphy for Congress on Facebook|url=https://www.facebook.com/325163984681739/posts/405953343269469/}} Walker responded in saying that God led his campaign to victory.{{cite web|title=Scott Walker for Congress on Facebook|url=https://www.facebook.com/188087995254191/posts/306316080098048/}} Student and community activist Andrew Webb declared his Republican write-in candidacy on September 17, 2018, hoping to gain support from dissatisfied Republicans. He announced a platform of more moderate/traditional conservative ideas.http://www.delawarepolitics.net/andrew-webb-launches-2018-campaign/ There are also two other write-in candidacies, with a far-right and conservative candidacy from Marvin Davis and Paul Johnston. ==Libertarian Party== ===Candidates=== ====Endorsed by Sussex County Chapter==== * Andrew Webb, community activist and student (write-in) ==American Independent Party== ===Candidates=== ====Write-in==== * Marvin Davis, far-rightist ==Independents== Not to be confused with the [[Independent Party of Delaware]], which currently has no candidate for the 2018 United States House of Representatives election. ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Paul Johnston, veteran (write-in) ====Withdrew==== * Christopher Mockerman, activist (running for [[Delaware House of Representatives|State House]] in District 17){{cite web|title=Source Voting - Delaware|url=https://www.sourcevoting.com/search/DE/1/house}} {{cite web|title=Declared Write-In Candidates - Delaware Department of Elections|url= https://elections.delaware.gov/pdfs/2018GeneralElectionDeclaredWriteInCandidates.pdf}} ==General election== ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box |title=Lisa Blunt Rochester |list= ;U.S. Senators *[[Tom Carper]], [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] from [[Delaware]] *[[Chris Coons]], U.S. Senator from Delaware ;Governors * [[John Carney (politician)|John Carney]], [[List of Governors of Delaware|74th Governor of Delaware]]https://www.instagram.com/p/Bn2Ihv8H4c4/?utm_source=ig_share_sheet&igshid=7iqm6n5n7c27 ;Lt.
